entry_conditions: Drawer is open and stable; target_pose is available; the block is plausibly held or is already over the cavity; the measured arm state admits a feasible approach in the assigned placement responsibility.
exit_conditions: The block rests inside the cavity at drawer-floor height and is detached; the TCP has retreated above the cavity and reached the fixture-relative handle approach for close_drawer.
overlap_role: All actions 680:1160 remain supervised. The 680:840 overlap with retrieval covers convergence into destination coordinates; the 900:1160 overlap with closing covers opening, settling, retreat, reorientation and handle approach/grasp.
successor_readiness: close_drawer may take over in 900:1160 only when two causal frames support a stationary floor-height block detached from the TCP. A late handoff occurs with the free gripper at the handle.
failure_signatures: target_pose jumps or is unavailable; object stops following the closed TCP before release; descent is outside the cavity; object remains suspended after opening; or IK residual/limit diagnostics show the shifted fixture target is unreachable.
continuation_guidance: Use place_block_in_drawer__h01 first if the attached entry block is far outside demonstrated destination-relative support. Use place_block_in_drawer__h03 for local release/retreat ambiguity. Otherwise retain this destination frame through the fixture-anchored transition and hand close_drawer only a settled object.
limitations: Destination displacement equivariance is a converter property, not observed rollout success. The goal pose must represent the drawer rigidly. Demonstrations do not include premature-drop recovery, and relative coordinates do not remove robot reachability or collision constraints.
